newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MGM forecasts EBIT at US$75.5 mln in 96 - paper.
newsitem.headline: MGM forecasts EBIT at US$75.5 mln in 96 - paper.

text.p: U.S. film and television studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM), recently bought by a consortium of Australia's Seven Network Ltd and U.S. investor Kirk Kerkorian, has forecast earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) in the year to December 31, 1996 of US$75.5 million, The Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper, quoting from what it said were internal MGM documents, said MGM's EBIT would then fall to US$55.2 million in 1997 and then rise back to US$89.5 million in 1998.

The forecasts were prepared in late 1995 or early 1996 before MGM completed a deal to supply the Showtime pay television channel with 325 hours of programmes in calendar 1997, the Australian Financial Review said.
"The MGM documents show that, prior to the Showtime deal, management had budgeted on US$121 million in television programme revenues in 1997," the newspaper said.
It said Seven Chairman Kerry Stokes had told the newspaper the Showtime deal would boost forecast revenues.

"While the 1996 forecast of earnings before interest and tax of US$75 million looks reasonable, Stokes says that the market would be unwise to rely too much on the later year forecasts," the Financial Review said.
"Stokes says that the Showtime deal should actually generate significantly higher television revenues in 1997 than the earlier forecasts suggest," the newspaper said.
Seven and Kerkorian's Tracinda Corp agreed in July to pay US$1.3 billion for the studio.
Seven's shares closed up one cent at A$3.88 on Tuesday.
